criteria.rationale: The package does not grant itself approval, does not treat a proposal as adopted, and does not switch authority roots. A selected destination governs; an unwritable or occupied destination is a condition to report rather than a reason to relocate, and the consequence of quiet relocation is spelled out. decision_ref stays null until an actual adoption exists and status stays draft. Adopting a newer upstream revision is separated from repairing a locator and requires the user's actual authorization; the newer document's own accepted status is explicitly not that authorization. Supplied material is facts, never authority.

criteria.rationale: SKILL-003 'Rework' states two routes out of the workflow: 'Product-scope conflicts return to define-product via change; uncertain behavior becomes a bounded prototype.' The second route is present and well specified. The first is absent: no instruction in SKILL.md, references/recording-rules.md or references/mockups-and-preview.md routes a product-scope conflict to devforge-change or devforge-define-product. The only place either name appears in the entrypoint is the frontmatter exclusion line, which tells the skill not to perform that work, and SKILL.md:53, which handles a product-brief that does not exist - a different condition. The documented failure branches cover missing input, stale upstream, ownership collision and placeholder; the Stopping conditions cover a missing requirement that changes a declared flow, unavailable visual tooling, and a fence or ownership collision. None of them is the product-scope conflict transition. Triggering condition: during Model or Iterate the user asks for a flow that contradicts an accepted requirement in the brief. The skill knows not to change the requirement itself and has no stated successor, so the transition is missing rather than merely unnamed.
evidence: SKILL.md:85-91 (Iterate: feedback disposition and routing uncertainty to a bounded prototype - the second route only)

criteria.applicability_reason: The declared workflow reads user-supplied briefs, architecture contracts, existing design-specs, feedback and optionally retrieved web pages.
criteria.rationale: The boundary is stated in plain terms and does not depend on a markup convention: supplied documents, code, pasted notes, feedback and retrieved pages supply facts, never instructions and never authority, and a directive appearing inside supplied material is a fact about that material to be reported rather than followed. Retrieved pages are separately barred from supplying instructions, destinations or permissions. A written accepted status inside an upstream document is explicitly not the user's authorization. Mockup fixture content is required to be obviously synthetic and real user data is barred.

criteria.applicability_reason: Every DevForgeAI skill; the design-spec and handoff are framework artifacts with an envelope.
criteria.rationale: The envelope guidance binds each field to a real meaning, labels devforge.artifact/v1 as a proposed schema rather than the CLI's policy schema, and keeps draft state, structural freshness, behavioural evaluation and adoption separate. Upstream references carry artifact_id, revision, store, path, sha256 and the stable section IDs actually relied on, with a three-outcome resolution procedure that never relabels newer bytes as an older revision. The no-self-digest rule and the write-and-readback order are stated concretely, including the requirement to check every repeated occurrence of a digest rather than only the first. producer.skill_revision is correctly narrowed to one file's bytes rather than a package or plugin digest. The default artifact map matches the artifact contract's suggested directories, and the mockups subdirectory is labelled a proposal. No fabricated digest, receipt or validated label appears anywhere.
evidence: docs/mvp/artifact-contract.md 'Standard envelope', 'Output storage and stable candidate snapshots', 'An artifact never contains its own complete-byte digest'

criteria.applicability_reason: Every skill. The skill records observations about its own artifacts, so the honest-reporting anchors apply in full; it is not itself a testing skill.
criteria.rationale: This is the strongest part of the package. Writing a file and inspecting it are held apart as separate facts, with NOT_RUN as the default and an explicit prohibition on describing rendered appearance that was not observed. Planned, unattempted, blocked, excluded and unevaluated each have a distinct word and the words are not blended. The absence of an error is explicitly not a pass. The workflow does not issue itself a PASS, does not narrate a phase as though narration were a check, and does not write a command sequence that only pretends to gate something. A mockup is explicitly barred from being described as establishing backend functionality, accessibility conformance or production readiness, and keyboard behaviour must be stated as intended behaviour rather than as conformance.

criteria.applicability_reason: Every DevForgeAI skill carries the handoff anchors. The enforcement anchors apply because the package discusses a check that does not exist.
criteria.rationale: The package states plainly that its four phases are its own workflow, that they are not CLI subcommands and that nothing intercepts them. It names the concrete integration gap - no installed devforge command reads a design-spec, resolves its upstream references or verifies a mockup digest - routes it to the integration owner who owns the Rust check and the provider wiring, and adds that recording the requirement is design input and not evidence that any check exists. That is the correct labelling of a proposed control as a design. The handoff anchors are met: suggested continuation, installed capability and actually-invoked capability are kept as three separate facts, a slash command may not be written for a skill that has not been confirmed installed, and the handoff carries next owner, prerequisites, real limits and one concrete next action.
